text_fidelity_a: SYMA Drone with Camera 1080P HD FPV Cameras Remote Control Toys RC Quadcopter Helicopter Gifts for Boys Girls Adults Beginners with Altitude Hold, Headless Mode, One Key Start, 3D Flips 2 Batteries I'm not much of a drone guy myself and if it were just for me, I'd have gotten bored with it a while ago, but my dogs LOVE it and for that alone it's worth the price. The drone is surprisingly durable, and has survived numerous bites and swats as the dogs chase it around the yard. It also came with spare rotors, which was a nice touch. I haven't needed them yet, but it's good to know they're there. Giving it 4 instead of 5 stars because it doesn't respond to controls like the instructions say it should. It luckily has a rudimentary collision detection system that helps it (sometimes) avoid obstacles, and it can ascend/descend well enough, but fine controls and steering are awkward at best. Still, for the price and for how well it stands up to abuse from the dogs, it's a winner!

Still the price was reasonable so I ordered one. This is not the first Klutz craft kit we've played with - so it was a familiar experience as those other kits. There really wasn't much in the box - the clay, a pencil (without an eraser), a sculpting tool, and a couple sheets of foldable paper props for the erasers you make (if you make the ones shown in the instructional guide).

You get plenty of different color clay - if you limit yourself to making fairly small erasers. The clay we got wasn't dried out - but it did take some kneeding to get soft enough to shape. Baking the erasers was simple - we used a toaster oven. Just be sure to use the right temperature and watch the erasers while they bake to make sure none start melting. Baking time can vary - mostly 15 to 30 minutes depending on the size & shape of the erasers you made.

The erasers are more ornamental than practical - but they do erase most pencil marks.

We're having fun with this kit - the instructional guide is outstanding. I'm happy with my purchase.

I do NOT recommend this for three-year-olds for two reasons. #1, I think the pieces are a Choking Hazard. #2, I really don’t think they are going to “get” the game. If you follow the instructions, I think it’s really WAY too complicated for such a young age. Granted, instead of playing the game, kids could just play with the pieces in other ways.

Finally, I think this item is WAY overpriced, at least at the current price, for a Made In China toy. If you can get it cheap, then you might want to pick it up.

It has a place to hold up to 6 cars when not in use. It takes some practice to get the car to crash into the middle, so it's not something that will happen automatically for most.

text_fidelity_a:
Magical Wizard Adventure – Fun Activities, Surprises, and Clues Magically Appear in an Enchanted Wizarding Book For this kit, you're paying for the convenience of having everything organized and already there. Also, for the "magical" experience you can provide for your child. If you do "Elf on a Shelf" or Santa Clause or anything similar, you'll probably love the added magical part of this kit. (We don't. We're all different and that's okay.) The parent has to be very involved. It's not a kit you just hand over to the child. (The parent portion is in a well sealed container to help keep the secret, since I imagine many parents will attempt to hand it straight over to the child. That was my plan before I realized what it was.) The child will have to do spells, and then the parent will secretly add activities to the wizard book. This is suppose to make the child believe their spell magically brought it to be. (For example: To get the first activity, the child will create a mix of sugar, salt, and 3 fragrant spices. They then go to the north side of their home, create a circle from the mix, and say the magic word 3 times. They then wait for the "magic"(parent) to bring the first activity to their book.)

The quality is similar to the various "Box of the Month" type subscriptions out there for kids, though I'd say this has more than average. It's not high quality, but it's still nice. The crafts are something that could be put together with supplies from a dollar store. But, it's so convenient having everything in one place, especially for a disorganized person, like myself. Plus, there are lots of codes and puzzles to solve, along with the "magical" experience provided for those that desire it.

Though I love Harry Potter, along with my 10 year old son, we were somewhat weirded out by the spells and all. (I truly thought we'd love this kit.) My child *really* didn't like that he was suppose to put a strand of his hair in the book for one part. We all have different comfort levels, but overall, this was out of our comfort level, especially mine. Still, we just took away parts we didn't like and tried to enjoy the rest. Unless you're super comfortable with doing spells and having runes and all, along with the pretending/lying(however you want to look at it) portion, this won't be the best kit for you and your child. I'd recommend going another direction. If you do love the thought of having runes and wands and saying spells, this will probably be a blast for you.
text_fidelity_b: Magical Wizard Adventure – Fun Activities, Surprises, and Clues Magically Appear in an Enchanted Wizarding Book

text_fidelity_a:
Luvabella Blonde Hair Interactive Baby Doll with Expressions & Movement (Ages 3+) Luvabella is quite an incredible doll, as the more your child plays with her, the more she learns and does. At first glance, she's quite plain, hard- not cuddly soft and has huge eyes with real eyelashes. The minute you put her 4 "C" batteries in (Doll does not come with batteries, you have to buy them), she comes to life with the cutest expressions, movements and baby babble speech. And incredibly, she speaks either English or French. (Coming from Canada, it's only natural- but of course she's made in China.)

Luvabella has a cute dress and hairbow, bottle, spoon, pacifier and lamb toy. When you give her the baby bottle, she easily goes to sleep, especially if you sing to her. When you feed her with the spoon, she chews and if you didn't feed her enough, she'll let you know. When she cries and gets fussy, waving her arms, her pacifier soothes her. Her lamb toy makes her make babble and animal sounds and the more she plays with the lamb, the more she learns more animal sounds and more animal names.

As the child plays with Luvabella, she does more and more. Touch her chest and hear her heart beat. Touch her feet, and she talks and calls you Mama. The baby babble will grow into words and eventually phrases. She even kisses her little Lamby toy and makes cute animal sounds. When you tickle her, she giggles and waves her arms. She plays peek-a-boo and laughs while you play with her, and eventually you'll hear her say "I see you". To have a conversation, hold her feet while speaking, she will answer back first in babble, then in words, then in phrases. As you speak and play with her, you never know what she'll do- either smile, cry, giggle or laugh. She constantly changes her responses and learns more vocabulary, and if your child gets tired of English, you can also hear her in French. This is a doll that gets cuter as she comes to life and keeps learning more, and your child will find her a wonderful challenge that never gets boring! A big 5 Stars for 2017.
text_fidelity_b: Luvabella Blonde Hair Interactive Baby Doll with Expressions & Movement (Ages 3+)

The instructions are clearly presented by pictures and words. While the written instructions contain some useful learning information, it is possible for kids to put them together without fully comprehending the reasons why. That being said, the written instructions feel age appropriate and try not to over complicate things which is really nice.

You don't have to (as my kid found out) but it's helpful. My kiddo routinely goes back to build and then explain why something works or doesn't. text_fidelity_a:
Chongker Stuffed Animals Handmade Realistic Black Cat Plush Companion Pet Gifts for Women Birthday Anniversary Cat Lover I've answered a few questions about this, so I will include this right away- this is only a plush (a really nice one)- it has no mechanical parts. It doesn't purr, or "breathe", makes no kitten or cat sounds, and therefore, requires no batteries.

This item was purchased as an "emotional support plushie", if you will. People need companionship, even folks who are no longer able to care for a living pet (or no longer wish to have the heartbreak of losing a real cat).

This fellow can absolutely be mistaken for a real cat at a distance. While being held and stroked, it's close enough to pass for a cat who is less than bunny-soft. The expressions and eyes are amazing, the little toe beans are soft silicone and give a little when squeezed. I couldn't have asked for more detail.

The care that went into creating this plush is evident in the details- from the examples in the pictures and video to those included from customer reviews (and those of the custom plushies are OUTSTANDING, I may have to treat myself to one someday!). It comes in a reusable case (resembling a cat carrier) with a little care booklet and grooming tool.

Personally I wouldn't give this plush to a young child (especially not one of the long-haired ones)- frankly, I'd be worried they'd damage it (squish things in the fur, allow the fur to become matted, color it with markers, cut the whiskers or fur...). Kids can be amazingly accidently destructive at times (we know they don't mean to, it just happens).

For me, the Chongker plush was well worth the price for the comfort it brings. I am quite seriously considering purchasing a custom colored one. I've seen the quality in the base product, and I'm confident in their ability to create good lookalike.
text_fidelity_b: Chongker Stuffed Animals Handmade Realistic Black Cat Plush Companion Pet Gifts for Women Birthday Anniversary Cat Lover

Ravensburger Dungeons, Dice & Danger – an Easy to Learn Roll and Write Strategy Game for Ages 12 and Up I have been enjoying this as a solo game but am happy that it won't be hard to teach friends.

Unlike some games there isn't a finite number of turns...the game ends when someone defeats the boss then each players points are tallied. I like that aspect a lot.

There are some "power" type blocks that benefit all players when one player has success with it.

The art is very cool and whimsical. The paper is sufficient but not very heavy duty. You get plenty of maps...there are 4 of each distinct map design. It's a busy map and I plan on taking the cheapest route possible and using regular sheet protectors and dry erase markers.

I'm not liking the wooden dice at all. For the money I would have really liked some fancier dice. Maybe bigger...maybe more colorful.
You get 4 short presharpened pencils that ...don't have erasers and your first game or two you might need to correct something.

Basically this could have been a print and play. There's nothing at all spectacular about the contents.

My personal little gripe is I don't see how you can be in two places at once. You can attack the map from different sides of the map moving in from starter sections.

That's seems like a lot of negativity but it is a fun little game anyway. You can play it on a small table or most places since there aren't components other than a map and the dice. Also this can encourage people to play who maybe aren't that into games since you don't unload tons of intimidating cards, counters and pieces.

It's a very fine experience. It could've been better for the money though.
text_fidelity_b: Ravensburger Dungeons, Dice & Danger – an Easy to Learn Roll and Write Strategy Game for Ages 12 and Up

He loves his cars and so this was a nice compact "repair garage" play structure. It will not be something you will want to break down daily and store, it will need to be up and available for immediate play. It will stay at my house for his visits and be stored on a closet shelf between visits. It came with one little tow truck vehicle. There is no car storage; this is just a play activity. A turning knob on top of the elevator brings cars up to individual floor levels and there are gates on the ramps that divert the cars to a car maintenance floor and a car wash floor in the structure. We were not interested in all the many decorative stickers that can be applied on this toy, so only used what we wanted to.

Educational Insights Shelby’s Snack Shack Game and Board Book Combo: Preschool Math Game, Board Game & Board Book, Ages 4+ We'd already bought the Sneaky Squirrel Game, which is similar to this game. We've though it was one of the cutest games ever, so we were thrilled to add this one to our collection, too!

With this game, you'll get one of the cutest boxes you've ever seen! (Let me note here that the top and bottom of the game box do NOT fit inside each other. It's the same with the squirrel game.) You'll also get a super cute pair of Shelby tweezers, 4 bowls, a packet of bones, and a double spinner.

Playing the game is pretty simple. There can be up to 4 players at a time. Each player will spin first to see if they will get bones or lose bones or just lose a turn. The second spin is to determine how many bones they will win/lose. If they land on a seagull, it means they will lose bones. If they land on the hungry pug, they get to steal bones from another player. Busy pug means they lose a turn, and landing on the bones mean they win bones for their bowl. They can pick up the bones they win/lose with the tweezers.

The tweezers are a great way to develop motor skills. The game itself is a great, fun way to learn counting skills. My 5 year old is delayed and really struggles with numbers, so I'm always thrilled to find a new, exciting way to teach them to him. This is also a fun game for my 2 year old. It IS pretty simple, so I imagine, on average, 2-4, maybe 5, is probably the best ages for this game.

Overall, this is a super cute game! I can highly recommend this AND the Sneaky Squirrel Game for your young little ones!
text_fidelity_b: Educational Insights Shelby’s Snack Shack Game and Board Book Combo: Preschool Math Game, Board Game & Board Book, Ages 4+

text_fidelity_a: Pussan Toys for 6+ Year Old Boys Car, Amphibious Remote Control Car, 2.4 GHz RC Stunt Car Toys 4WD Off-Road Trucks, Birthday Gift for 6-12 Kids Boys Girls, Beach and Water Toys for Children This is a fun 4wd car to drive.  It runs pretty fast on the 6 volt NiCd battery.  It is nearly impossible to roll it over and get it stuck as it just flips over and keeps on going.  Battery life is good (20 to 30 mins).  Controller is a bit small for adult hands but fits my 12 year old granddaughter hands very well.  The car is not DIgitally controlled (its all on or all off- no proportional steering or throttle), but it is able to spin around while staying in place (think tank or dozer like and you get the idea).  Have not had a chance to run it in the water yet as it has been real dry here the last couple weeks.  I tested it on a mowed lawn and gravel driveway and it will handle these surfaces ok.  The plastic tires are getting a little chewed up from the gravel so do be aware that a constant gravel use will probably wear out the tires.  Also tried it on wood and carpet and it runs great on those surfaces.  It comes with a handy phillips screwdriver to take out the 4 (YES 4!) battery cover screws.  I'm guessing so many screws to help keep the battery dry when running in water.  Didn't try out the charging cord as the USB cords are nothing more than a trickle charger and take too long.  I used my B6 V2 chargerer and the battery comes out a little under spec (typical).  Remote takes 2 AA batteries.  Car is fun but there is no suspension and hard plastic tires make for a very stiff drive.  I normally run off road rock crawlers in a dry creek bed so this car really isn't designed for that type of use, but for smooth surface running this is a good fun choice.
text_fidelity_b: Pussan Toys for 6+ Year Old Boys Car, Amphibious Remote Control Car, 2.4 GHz RC Stunt Car Toys 4WD Off-Road Trucks, Birthday Gift for 6-12 Kids Boys Girls, Beach and Water Toys for Children

text_fidelity_a:
Crayola DigiTools Paint Pack Okay first off -- you can just download the app for this product in your Apple or Android app store. It will be somewhat limited, including having some of the "backgrounds" aka digital coloring pages disabled. There are more than one DigiTools apps - I was able to unlock two of the currently available four with this set: Their paint app and their airbrush app. Other sets that include different tools can unlock the other two (including a 3D set). The App consists of the backgrounds and several solid colored canvases. Using the appropriate tool allows you to do things like paint, stamp included images onto your scene, roll paint or images along your painting. Staying true to the Crayola kid friendly tradition the app doesn't include any sort of advanced features (no layers, etc). Your tools, an eraser, and an undo button are all you will find here.

The tools (what you're really buying here) consists of a Stamper, a roller, a brush, and an airbrush. Basically all of these (except the brush) are just several stylus nubs embedded into plastic tools that are kid friendly. The brush looks just like a run of the mill cheap brush (I can see kids grabbing it to paint with for real so look out for that) but when you hold it properly it too works like a stylus.

If you or the kids graduate out of the app and decide that say they do want to use them on more advanced programs? Good news and bad news there... The good news is that since these are basically just kid friendly tablet tools, yes these work in others apps. The bad news is that if you plan to say drag the stamper across your screen to get three lines at once? That's not going to happen. The screen will see this same as if you are using two fingers at once. So, for example, when I used these tools in Sketchbook pro? The brush worked perfectly. The airbrush and roller tools worked IF I tilted them so that only one nub was touching the screen at a time (otherwise it thought I was trying to pinch in and out / zoom). The stamper tool, which has three nubs, was basically useless.

The brush (the most useful tool in the pack) is also what makes this overall a 4 not a 5 star tool. The bristles are very fragile, I used this set a couple of times, put them away in the included carrying case, went to draw again and hmm the bristles were all fanned out and bent back. I don't know that the brush will hold up long term, it's already the most finicky tool in the set. Still, a fun kid friendly set that adults will love too.
text_fidelity_b: Crayola DigiTools Paint Pack

Winning Moves Games Winning Moves No Stress Chess, Natural (1091) for 2 players My daughter (8 years) really took an interest in a chess a few years ago. We played regular chess, but it wasn't that engaging. This levels the playing field and is really fun, even if you understand play chess a lot. The game focuses on drawing cards that tell you want piece to move. Based on the card, it poses different scenarios that either level the playing field or draws the game a bit longer. For example, being in check and not drawing a king card to move out or not drawing a card to neutralize the check. My daughter had made some gear combos with the pieces in her hand. There are really three modes

(1) each player draws one card and that is the card to move. (Easiest)
(2) each player has 3 cards and plays a piece from that
(3) each player has 5 cards and plays a piece from one of those cards

I'm surprised this hasn't been invented before. It is great if you've never played chess or have played chess and want to teach someone new.
text_fidelity_b: Winning Moves Games Winning Moves No Stress Chess, Natural (1091) for 2 players

text_fidelity_a:
Logo Party Board Game "Logo Party" gives players the chance to guess famous logos in a variety of ways. Depending on what type of card you draw, you will try to have other players guess the logo by drawing the clues (like Pictionary), acting out the item (as in Charades), or describing the brand (like the old game show "Pyramid".) Players have twenty seconds to guess the brand from the clues provided. Each team has a token to move around the board and try to get to the end first by guessing more brands than the other team. The game includes a tablet for the drawing clues and a box to hold the cards during play and for storage. Unfortunately, the box is too small and the cards don't fit well.

The game is designed for four or more players divided into two teams. The recommended ages are listed as eight and up, but most eight-year-olds would be unfamiliar with many of the brands featured in the game. In fact, even older teens and adults won't know some of these brands. Also, I would call some of the items products and not brands. For example, one of the "brands" is Chicken McNuggets (as opposed to McDonald's.)

The game is somewhat fun, but would be much better with a large group of people. My family found it almost impossible to act out most of the brands, but it was funny to see people try to act things out like "Tupperware". With more people, I'm sure it would be even funnier.

Throughout the boards, there are spaces called, "Reveal It". When landing on this space, players from both teams try to guess a brand by looking at the logo. This is also how the winner is ultimately determined when teams reach the end of the game board. The timer that comes with the game doubles as a holder for these cards. The card starts out fully covered and then parts of the brand are slowly revealed. This is a clever idea, but it's hard to place the card in the holder without looking at. Also, it makes an annoying buzzing sound (like the sound of a small wind-up toy.) Because of the sound, we used a different timer during regular play and saved the timer for the "Reveal It" cards.

The game would be more fun for a large group of people. My family had some fun playing "Logo Party", but got bored after a while since some of the brands were unknown to some of the players and it was hard to act out the brands and actually get someone to guess them.
text_fidelity_b: Logo Party Board Game

While I would have loved (although not necessarily expected) some karate-chop action in the parent figures, or flamethrower accessories, this is a pretty cool looking fortress, no wait, I mean dollhouse, and my daughter loves it, even if she doesn't understand why GI Joe keeps trying to rappel up to the 4th floor balcony with his grappling hook. .

Everything that she wants to play with is, of course, something I have to buy separately. That's a bit annoying, but typical I suppose, although someone with more experience in these sorts of girl-fortresses might know of a better alternative. Practically speaking, Cobra Commander and Skelator could just waltz right in the front door, as there are no missile launchers, so those must come in one of the accessory packs.

At the end of the game, who ever has the most victory points wins.

text_fidelity_a:
Fisher-Price Roar 'n Ride Lion [[VIDEOID:6d6cbfe820d25c4bf20272caa9cdc5e0]] My girlfriend said, "This is the kind of toy that you only get for your worst enemies." I, on the other hand love it! And, kids love it too. The problem with this is that it's a noise-making toy that is very fun and exciting if you're the one controlling it, but kind of annoying if you're not controlling it.

This is a play lion, that comes with suction cups to stick to the side of the car. When you press the lion's belly, then it makes some sounds. When you rattle something, like with the attached rattle, then it does extended music and sound. It's meant to teach kids that if they rattle something, then something else in the environment might react.

One big warning. This ships in Demo mode, where pressing the Lion's tummy works, but the rattle doesn't work. At first I thought it was broken. But, all you have to do is switch this off and then switch it back on, and then both the rattle and pressing the Lion's abdomen will work. And, speaking of switching this off, the switch is hidden on the lion's back, and is super hard to get to. And, it's impossible to change the batteries without ripping the lion's clothes.

Pros:
+Kids love it
+Great for teaching cause and effect
+Makes a lot of noise
+You can stick it on the window

Cons:
-Can be annoying for adults
-On/off switch and batteries are inconveniently located
-Isn't as fun if it's not stuck to a window
text_fidelity_b: Fisher-Price Roar 'n Ride Lion

text_fidelity_a: Monterey LG8510 Lady Bug Lure, Pack of 3 I buy these lures each year ever since I learned that ladybugs like to cluster in small hollow space in houses. One year I had 1 exterior wall with over 1000 ladybugs crawling on it in the sunshine, a day later they were all gone and over the following weeks they started falling out of the cracks inside my house. Every morning as soon as the sun rose I would start finding them everywhere. I checked the internet and found the Ladybuglady who told me that ladybugs cluster in the late fall to stay warm through the winter. If they find a space like a house and a way in they will literally take over the sun side wall of the house. The way to avoid this was to build ladybug houses (similar to bird house but with smaller holes) and place them in your garden and orchards where the Ladybugs will benefit your plants (they eat aphids) and get these lures to draw them to the houses. Well for 2 years it has worked like a charm. No ladybugs in my houses and the trees in my orchard are doing very well.
text_fidelity_b: Monterey LG8510 Lady Bug Lure, Pack of 3

Alex Discover Snap-to-It Ocean Game Kids Art and Craft Activity My grandson is almost three years old, and I thought he’d enjoy this toy...that was until I received it. Upon first inspection you notice a cheaply made zip-up half circle that opens to expose rivets that a child is supposed to insert the enclosed plastic big “buttons”. Let me just tell you that there’s no way that my grandson can attach these things to the mat - it took all my strength and dexterity to get one or two to pop in place. This is simply too difficult for a child of any age and not challenging but frustrating. Then there’s these cute little ocean-themed felt cut-outs that you’re supposed to “hook” around the installed buttons. They’re brightly colored and my grandson did enjoy taking them off and on the buttons for about 15 minutes. Then there’s a few pieces of string...some are about 4” long (too short to practice tying and really too short for a toddler to attempt to thread through four holes on the felt pieces) and others are about 6” long. ALSO, Within fifteen minutes of play my toddler was pulling on the buttons attempting to remove them and the rivets we’re poppong off and the mat was falling apart, not to mention the tiny metal circles all over the floor were now a choking hazard and the mat no longer works in the holes that lost the rivets.

Overall PROs- cute felt pieces that easily attach much like a button hole that toddler can practice with.
CONs-cheap plastic sewn mat, hard to attach buttons, useless strings, mat falling apart during first play.

Prextex Pack of 2 Wind up Bubble Machine Toy Gun Shooter LED Light up Bubbles Blower Indoor and Outdoor Toys for Kids and Toddler - no Batteries Needed | Great Gift Set for Birthdays I bought two packs of these bubble guns for a birthday party. You receive 2 pink guns and 3 blue guns in each pack. They are clear and have noise and lights.

Of the 10 bubble guns I received, 2 were defective. There is a lever that moves up and down to produce the bubbles. The lever is supposed to move when the trigger is pressed. For one of the defective bubble guns the lever was so tight that it rarely moved hence no bubbles. For the second defective bubble gun the rubber tubing was run the wrong way down the front of the gun so the rubber tube is very short. It produces bubbles but only when immersed in liquid in the bottle. It also spills a large amount of bubble liquid because of the defective tubing. After a short while it stops working because the bubble solution is too low in the bottle. My hand was also covered in solution at this point.

For the remainder of the bubble guns the rubber tubing is too long and they will not produce bubbles. The tubing is pressed against the side of the bubble container and is unable to siphon up the bubble liquid. The solution is to either push the tubing back up into the gun to make it about 1/4 inch shorter or to snip the end of the tubing by about 1/8 inch. The remaining 8 guns worked after I pushed the tubing higher.

I recommend you test the guns before handing them to children. I bought them for a birthday party so I tested them ahead of time to prevent disappointment.

These are different than battery operated bubble guns. For one thing, the lever has to be pressed about three times each time to produce bubbles in most of the bubble guns. For a few of the bubble guns a slow steady press produced a steady stream of bubbles but most of the triggers are too loose to allow a slow press. So the quality is inconsistent.

I paid $15.99 per box so from a value perspective I wasted about $6.36 because of the defective guns. I'll probably return one box.

UPDATE: Amazon shipped two replacement boxes but 5 of the 10 replacement guns were defective. I could not get them to work no matter how hard or long I tried. I shipped the defective bubble guns back. I will repeat my advice. Test each gun if you are using them for a party or event. Buy early enough so you have time to have replacements shipped to you. The ones that did work, worked beautifully. The kids enjoyed them.
text_fidelity_b: Prextex Pack of 2 Wind up Bubble Machine Toy Gun Shooter LED Light up Bubbles Blower Indoor and Outdoor Toys for Kids and Toddler - no Batteries Needed | Great Gift Set for Birthdays
